description: Pre-Columbian Zapotec polity centred on the hilltop city of Monte Albán above the modern Mexican city of Oaxaca, with a continuous occupation from roughly 500 BCE through to the ninth century. At its Classic peak Monte Albán housed perhaps 25,000 residents and exercised regional dominance across the Oaxaca Valley through a network of fortified secondary centres. Its decline from around 700 onward preceded political fragmentation across the valley and the postclassic Mixtec ascendancy at Mitla and elsewhere.

temporal.notes: Classic Zapotec urban civilisation centred on Monte Albán above the Oaxaca Valley; political authority at the site contracted sharply by ~850, after which power dispersed to Mitla, Yagul, and smaller centres.
